correctness.rationale: For fixed direction the support is the maximum of two affine face supports; pairing opposite directions gives (4). Under the uniform three-dimensional sphere the absolute axial cosine is uniform and independent of the transverse azimuth. The positive-part integral gives (1) exactly, not asymptotically. Uniform convergence near zero gives all positive even moments. Hausdorff compact-moment determinacy for positive support values yields the iff inverse. Affine support maxima give convexity in taper, reflection makes the expectation even, Jensen establishes strictness, and central symmetry gives pointwise order. Standalone numerical regression is corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: A naturally controlled one-dimensional family of unlabeled mean-width experiments exactly classifies the support-value distribution of an arbitrary planar convex base, specifies the nonidentifiable angular information, yields all even moments constructively, and gives a sharp local quadratic response.
